articles.title: Rupee falls 11 paise to 96.36 against US dollar in early trade
articles.content: The rupee fell eleven paise to 96.36 against the US dollar on Wednesday. Crude oil prices climbed due to geopolitical tensions and shipping concerns. Domestic equity markets experienced a slight downturn on Wednesday.

articles.title: US House passes stopgap funding bill to avert shutdown before midterm elections
articles.content: The US House approved a temporary funding bill to keep government agencies operational. This measure extends federal funding through December 4, averting a shutdown. Republicans advanced the legislation early to manage their legislative calendar. Democrats largely opposed the bill, citing a lack of bipartisan negotiation. The move aims to allow more time for appropriations and defense spending discussions.

articles.title: FIIs just pumped $3 billion into Indian stocks as brutal selloff ends. Here's what they are buying
articles.content: Foreign investors have injected nearly $3 billion into Indian equities recently. Financial services and consumer services attracted significant inflows from these investors. However, automobiles and power sectors experienced substantial outflows during this period. This renewed buying is seen as tactical, not a broad market rebuilding. Global macroeconomic shifts and valuations continue to influence foreign investment decisions.

articles.title: Global developed market debt to hit record $75.8 trillion by end of 2026: Fitch
articles.content: Government debt in developed nations will reach $75.8 trillion by 2026. This debt burden represents 104% of gross domestic product for these countries. Major global shocks and rising spending pressures contribute to this significant increase. Higher borrowing costs and defense budgets also add to the growing debt. Artificial intelligence may offer economic growth but also presents new fiscal challenges.

articles.title: Tata Group stock falls 2% after Q1 net profit jumps 18% to Rs 390 crore
articles.content: Indian Hotels Company reported a 18.5% net profit rise in Q1 FY27.  Revenue per available room increased fourteen percent at domestic hotels. Despite disruptions, IHCL maintained its double-digit revenue growth guidance.
